items.title: Chuck Mancuso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 10, 2013
items.q: And I remember B.B. King said, “Thank God for Charlie Keil.”

ctx.x: No that’s fine. This art thing. What has to happen for an American popular music style to get to the level of being considered an art form? I mean jazz did. Is blues an art form, and why so?

Well I don’t know what the parameters of how you define an art form, but I think when more and more historian/critics start doing real heavy research and they see there are connections to many other areas, not necessarily Matisse and the French Impressionists movement, because these were mostly uneducated guys and gals doing blues. But the fact that the records were important. Today they call it roots music. I was calling it underground music. But it’s all underground, you know, building up. So I think when the…

my rock & roll class we do the lost highways. You know, here’s what these guys were traveling. Then you had the white guys, Merle Haggard and these guys who went out to California, you know, first picking grapes and then potatoes, and then you had the black guys who were going to their various places, first Chicago and then later California. And then you have Charles Brown and Nat Cole. He could play piano. And they had those independent record companies. Oh my God. What a world. And I get to teach about it. And…
